the app auto-generates a branch graph (no manual quick command needed):

Trimming is stable in plain transcode mode (no watermark/PiP) and supports fast (keyframe-based) and accurate (decoded-frame) trimming.

When 'Watermark' or 'PiP (sub-video)' is also enabled:
  Main video trim:
   - 'Accurate trim' (check 'frame-accurate') is recommended so watermark duration matches exactly.
   - Fast mode is keyframe-based, so end time may drift a few frames (usually negligible).
  Sub-video (watermark/PiP) trim:
   - The trimmed clip loops via the loop filter until the main video ends.
   - With a finite loop count, an enable expression limits show time; the watermark disappears after N loops, main video continues.
   - Infinite or over-long loop keeps the watermark until the end.

If you do not want looping or need finer control, prepare the sub-video on the 'Transcode' tab first, then import it as watermark/PiP material.

Combined-seek mode (recommended only for a single clean video transcode)

Idea: first jump fast to the keyframe before the target (input seek), then decode precisely to the target frame (output seek) - speed and accuracy together.

Threshold meaning:
  e.g. start 3600s, threshold 30s -> pre-seek 3570s, post fine-tune 30s

When to use:
  - A single video, no overlay / watermark / PiP
  - Need to trim from the middle of a long video (e.g. from 1h)
  - Encoder not copy (must re-encode)

Enable when: total > 2 min AND start > 30s. For short clips (<5 min) or early start (<10s) the gain is small.

Do NOT use:
  - Watermark or PiP enabled (auto-disabled): the trailing -ss cannot tell main from sub video, causing mis-trim.
  - Frame-accurate mode (mutually exclusive; auto-unchecked)
  - Audio-only extraction

Speed-up (2h movie, trim from 1h):
  - Software decode: saves ~15-30 min
  - HW decode (cuda/qsv): saves ~5-10 min
  - Accurate trim decodes everything before discarding, so it is slow

Threshold tip: default 30s covers most keyframe intervals (1-10s); do not raise it, or decoding grows.

You can add FFmpeg CLI params directly.

[Smart filter merge]
- A bare filter string (e.g. drawtext=text='hello':x=10:y=10) is auto-detected as video/audio and inserted/replaced at the right place in the generated -vf/-af chain.
- Strings prefixed with -vf / -af / -filter_complex also merge smartly instead of overwriting.
- Same-name filters replace by default (e.g. scale=1920:-2 replaces the UI's scale=1280:-2), except drawtext / subtitles / overlay which stack, allowing multiple text watermarks.

- Non-filter params (-x264-params, -bsf, -t, -map ...) are appended as-is at the end.
- Do not re-add params already on the UI (tune, profile, level, maxrate, bufsize) to avoid conflict.

- Appending custom -t forces output length, a safeguard against infinite output from filter loops (main watermark mode). Or use -t 10 for a 10s preview; the preview command may not pass all filters, especially watermarks (placeholder box only).

- setsar=1 forces SAR 1:1, good with square scale: e.g. 400x400 compresses a 16:9 frame correctly.

[Stream copy mode (encoder = copy)]

- Audio speed/reverse are independent per track; trim is per audio track.
